title: POC plan: Edge residency & PrivateLink vs Peering
summary: Discovery/PoC scoping for running Redwood Private in NexaGen's regulated workloads. Main decision: PrivateLink vs VPC peering for cross-account private connectivity, plus region residency and egress controls. Success criteria include p99 latency < 120ms for 1k concurrent requests (avg prompt 600 tokens), deterministic audit logs, KMS integrated encryption, and no cross-region egress. Timeline: 6-week pilot with benchmark week in week 3.
topics: Connectivity options: VPC Peering vs PrivateLink vs Transit Gateway
Workload sizing: tokens/sec, concurrency, batching and GPU counts
Benchmarks: latency p50/p95/p99, throughput (tokens/sec), cost per 1k reqs
Data residency & egress restrictions, region locking
Security controls: KMS/HSM, SOC2, audit logs, SSO/SAML
Pilot timeline, success criteria, next steps
next_steps: Redwood to share Private Networking guide + sample CloudFormation for Privatelink by 2026-12-18
NexaGen to provide current traffic profile (avg tokens per request, 95th perc concurrency) by 2026-12-20
Schedule benchmark week (3rd week of pilot) — target dates proposed: 2027-01-11 to 2027-01-15
Security team review: NexaGen to run initial compliance questionnaire and Redwood to supply SOC2 + ISO docs by 2026-12-22

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: 58m | Recording: yes 
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Sam Ortega (CTO - NexaGen), Jordan Patel (Cloud Infra), Leah Rivera (Security), Ravi Menon (ML Platform)

Summary (auto): Discussed PoC scope to validate private networking options and residency controls. Agreed pilot length, initial bench plan. Action items captured.

00:00 Alex (AE): hey everyone thanks for making time, um we'll run through the scope and make sure we align on success criteria for the POC  
00:18 Sam (CTO): yes thanks — we've had a couple outages with current vendor and they leaked tokens across acccounts so security is first. we need region lock to eu-west-2 and no egress across accounts or regions  
00:33 Priya (SE): totally understood. for Redwood Private we can do VPC peering or AWS Privatelink, or use a TGW approach, each has tradeoffs on routing and egress policies 
00:47 Jordan (Infra): quick Q — peering means peering across accounts right? we have a central networking account with TGW already, not keen on open routes to other accounts  
01:02 Priya (SE): yes vpc peering is route table level — you can control with NACLs/security groups but it does become a two-way route; PrivateLink is endpoint-based and is uni-directional from your VPC to the service endpoint which gives tighter egress control  
01:21 Sam (CTO): ok so PrivateLink sounds safer for us but what's perf like? our workloads are latency sensitive — targeting p99 <120ms for prompt lengths ~600 tokens with 250 reqs/s concurrency bursts to 1k  
01:41 Marcus (SE): good callout, we need to size GPU footprint and batching. for 600-token avg prompts at 250 concurrent steady state you likely want a pool of at least 8 A100-ish instances for throughput-oriented models; quantized Llama variants push that down. benchmarks are the way to confirm 
02:03 Ravi (ML): our current metrics: avg tokens/request ~620, median latency w/ current provider ~210ms but with high variance; we usually do short-term batching window of 30ms in our infra  
02:20 Priya (SE): ok we'll design a benchmark that runs three profiles: low latency (batch 0-10ms), balanced (batch 30ms), throughput (batch 100ms) and capture p50/p95/p99 and tok/sec. also measure cold-start for KV cache misses  
02:42 Jordan (Infra): if we pick PrivateLink does that force the model to be in your account? how do we ensure no cross-region traffic?  
02:57 Marcus (SE): PrivateLink endpoints are regional; you can advertise endpoint only in eu-west-2 and we won't route outside that AZ/region. we'll also lock the service to your account via endpoint policies so egress to other accounts is prevented.  
03:16 Leah (Security): we need to see audit logs for each request — request id, model version, who called it, and retained logs for 13 months. KMS integration is mandatory, and we require HSM-backed keys for production  
03:36 Priya (SE): Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS; HSM notes use a KMS with external key management — we'll provide an integration guide. audit logs available via consolidated logging to your SIEM (we stream to CloudWatch/ELK). retention and export policies configurable  
03:56 Sam (CTO): on success criteria — aside from latency — we want determinism on model outputs for our regression prompts. If the model drift exceeds thresholds on rouge/semantic sims we're failing the POC  
04:12 Ravi (ML): yes we have a test set of 1.5k prompts (PHI-scrubbed) we'll use for quality regression, and we need stable quantized model artifacts. can Redwood pin model versions and provide diff logs?  
04:29 Priya (SE): absolutely. model pinning + rollout policies are supported. we can capture outputs for each run and provide diffs; we'll include a quality-monitoring hook in the benchmark plan  
04:42 Jordan (Infra): network egress question — if we do peering across accounts with TGW, how do we prevent accidental route propagation?  
04:55 Marcus (SE): TGW can be configured with route tables and propagation disabled, but it adds administrative overhead; PrivateLink gives narrower attack surface and simpler ACLs 
05:08 Sam (CTO): cost is a factor. is PrivateLink materially more expensive than peering?  
05:18 Alex (AE): there are endpoint hourly costs plus data processing fees on AWS; peering has no AWS endpoint cost but may increase latency and require more network ops. we'll include example TCO scenarios in the pricing sheet  
05:35 Leah (Security): SOC2 and ISO docs please — and a diagram showing where logs are stored and who can access keys.  
05:45 Marcus (SE): will add in package. also note we can offer a dedicated capacity plan if you want strict tenancy for the pilot  
05:53 Sam (CTO): timeline thoughts? we need pilot done before product freeze Feb 15 so we can decide for compliance board on Feb 21  
06:03 Priya (SE): workable: propose 6-week pilot starting Jan 4. week 1 onboarding & infra config, week 2 connectivity and smoke tests, week 3 benchmark week, week 4 tuning, week 5 security & compliance validation, week 6 wrap + exec review  
06:22 Jordan (Infra): Jan 4 is rough on our side (holiday rot), can we start Jan 11 instead?  
06:30 Alex (AE): yes shifting a week is fine — so Jan 11 to Feb 21 timeline fits with your freeze  
06:38 Sam (CTO): metrics for success — 1) p99 latency under 120ms for baseline profile, 2) throughput >= tokens/sec target for 250 sustained concurrency, 3) audit & KMS integrated, 4) quality regression pass < 2% drift on landmark prompts  
06:55 Priya (SE): we'll formalize the acceptance criteria in the benchmark playbook. also planning to run a small canary with 5% traffic once validated  
07:06 Leah (Security): about canary — we need RBAC controls and per-token masking on logs, plus ability to redact any PHI before logs leave your environment  
07:20 Marcus (SE): we have a redaction hook — logs can be processed through a lambda that scrubs tokens, and the full request bodies can be kept in your account encrypted with your KMS  
07:31 Ravi (ML): for workload sizing, what's the recommended GPU type? we're using mix of T4 and A10 now but will consider A100 if needed  
07:45 Priya (SE): for deterministic low-latency with 600-token prompts at p99 target, an A100-class node or equivalent (8k vram-ish) is recommended. If you go quantized 4-bit Llama-variant you can run more on A10s but will trade a bit on output fidelity — we should include fidelity checks in the bench plan  
08:05 Jordan (Infra): what about KV cache warming and session affinity? our calls are multi-turn and cache hit-rate impacts latency a lot  
08:18 Marcus (SE): we'll test both cold starts and warmed cache. Redwood runtime supports sticky sessions / affinity and warm KV sharing across workers in the same pool — we can configure cache TTLs  
08:33 Alex (AE): any legal/procurement blocker we should know of?  
08:38 Leah (Security): standard NDAs ok. legal will want a Data Processing Agreement showing residency and processing boundaries — add that to docs pack  
08:49 Priya (SE): will include DPA template and compliance pack  
08:52 Sam (CTO): ok bring me back to the PrivateLink vs Peering practical summary, please  
09:00 Priya (SE): PrivateLink: endpoint-based, uni-directional, stronger egress control, small added AWS costs, simpler RBAC & policies. VPC Peering: cheaper on AWS bills, but two-way routes and more network ops to lockdown, may require TGW to scale across many accounts. For NexaGen with strict residency and egress, PrivateLink recommended  
09:24 Jordan (Infra): TGW could be used if we want central control, but I like PrivateLink for the POC to minimize blast radius  
09:31 Alex (AE): decision: try PrivateLink for pilot; if we need TGW later for scale, revisit  
09:38 Sam (CTO): agreed. let's formalize success criteria and runbook  
09:44 Priya (SE): next steps recap: we'll share benchmark plan, private networking CFN, KMS integration notes, SOC2 + ISO docs and pricing pilot estimate. you share traffic profile and VPC layout.
09:58 Alex (AE): thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for Jan 11 kickoff and the benchmark week.

Notes on transcript quality: some words mis-typed by auto-transcription (Privatelink vs PrivateLink, vpc peerng), speaker attribution occasionally coarse.
notes: Customer emphasized non-negotiable data residency (eu-west-2), HSM-backed KMS, and audit retention of 13 months. PrivateLink chosen for pilot due to egress control. Pilot shifted to Jan 11 start. Benchmark week scheduled mid-pilot. Redwood will supply docs & CFN examples.
